signals.title: Burkina Faso : mandats d'arrêt contre des journalistes et activistes en exil pour faits de "terrorisme"
signals.summary: Les autorités du Burkina Faso ont annoncé avoir lancé des mandats d’arrêt contre une vingtaine de personnes en exil et demandé leur extradition. Des journalistes et un ancien pilier du régime de Blaise Compaoré sont notamment visés.

signals.title: COP31: le président malgache réclame des milliards de dollars et promet 85% d’énergies renouvelables
signals.summary: À la COP31, en Turquie, Madagascar réclame des milliards de dollars pour faire face au changement climatique. Le colonel Michaël Randrianirina promet, en échange, une baisse substantielle des émissions de gaz et 85 % d’énergies renouvelables, d’ici 2030, des engagements qui laissent sceptiques les défenseurs de l’environnement à Madagascar.

signals.title: Orpaillage en Guinée: les affrontements dans la région de Siguiri suscitent des critiques
signals.summary: Les réactions se multiplient après les morts de manifestants à Bouré-Balato mercredi, dans la région aurifère de Siguiri. L’interdiction de l’orpaillage artisanal le 2 novembre a tourné à l’affrontement entre des orpailleurs et les forces de défense et de sécurité, faisant au moins 10 morts selon un bilan provisoire du gouvernement.

signals.title: Niger: plus de 30 civils tués dans une attaque près de Téra, dans la région de Tillabéri
signals.summary: Au Niger, une attaque a eu lieu jeudi 12 novembre dans la région de Tillabéri, dans l'ouest du pays, épicentre des violences terroristes. Elle s'est produite près de la localité de Téra, proche du Burkina Faso et du Mali. Pas de communication ni de bilan officiels à ce stade. Des sources locales jointes par l'Agence France-Presse avancent le chiffre d'au moins 37 morts.

signals.title: Massacre de Shakahola au Kenya : dans les coulisses de l’enquête de Jeune Afrique
signals.summary: Le 6 novembre, le pasteur kényan Paul Mackenzie a été condamné à 200 ans de prison pour le meurtre de 191 personnes. À l’occasion de ce verdict, Jeune Afrique revient sur les coulisses de son documentaire sur l’engrenage mortel qui a mené à ce massacre inédit.

signals.title: Mozambique: Mondlane trial in 45-seat courtroom, country’s first with audio and video recording of hearings
signals.summary:
The trial of Venâncio Mondlane, in connection with the post-election demonstrations, begins on Tuesday, with five charges remaining, including terrorism. It will be the first trial in Mozambique to feature video and audio recording of court hearings, reducing the length of proceedings. “It is the first trial, and I think we should make a point…

signals.title: Simandou Mining Summit : la Guinée présente 3,8 milliards de dollars de projets aux investisseurs internationaux
signals.summary:
Envoyé spécial à Conakry
La première édition du Simandou Mining Summit, organisée du 11 au 14 novembre 2026 à Conakry, a réuni 2 240 participants venus de 41 pays, selon les organisateurs. Au-delà de la mobilisation des grands groupes miniers internationaux, le rendez-vous aura surtout permis de présenter aux investisseurs quatre projets prioritaires représentant 3,8 milliards de dollars. Une première traduction opérationnelle des ambitions de diversification économique…

signals.title: Nigeria: Folawiyo’s T1 Marine battles revenue authority over $1.2m tax demand
signals.summary: Billionaire Tunde Folawiyo’s T1 Marine Services is locked in an eight-year legal battle with the Nigeria Revenue Service over disputed ₦1.65bn tax assessments and ₦2.88bn in disallowed business expenses.

signals.title: Mozambique: Sant’Egidio reports brutal murder of 15-year-old Juvêncio, his 12-year-old friend Ilton still missing
signals.summary:
A 15-year-old boy has been killed and another, aged 12, has been missing since Saturday in the Mozambican city of Matola, in the south of the country, the Sant’Egidio Community reported this Friday (13 November), linking the cases to superstitious beliefs and calling for a swift investigation. According to Father Rolando Curzi, a priest with…

signals.title: Cyberattacks turned October into a costly month for Nigerian banks
signals.summary: In early October, a wave of cyberattacks, leading to fraud losses, hit several Nigerian banks and financial institutions, potentially costing billions of naira in customer funds, according to several sources with direct knowledge of the matter.

signals.title: Transporters Warn Alcohol Bill Could Put Sh14.6bn Freight Revenue At Risk
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Proposed restrictions on the transportation of alcoholic beverages could put up to Sh14.6 billion in annual freight revenue at risk, with transporters warning that the measures could disrupt supply chains, increase logistics costs and threaten thousands of jobs.

signals.title: Tsema Receives Nedc Relief Items for Attack Victims
signals.summary: [Leadership] The North-East Development Commission (NEDC), has donated food and non-food relief materials to the Taraba State Government for distribution to families affected by recent attacks in the state.

signals.title: Co-Op Bank Commits Sh1.5bn to Electric Matatu Financing
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Co-operative Bank has set aside Sh1.5 billion to finance the acquisition of electric public service vehicles (PSVs), targeting matatu Savings and Credit Co-operative Societies (Saccos) as the country seeks to accelerate the shift away from fossil-fuel-powered transport.

signals.title: 5 Killed, 1 Missing After Building Collapses Near Syokimau SGR Road
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Five people have been confirmed dead and another reported missing after a building under construction partially collapsed along the SGR Syokimau access road in Nairobi on Friday morning.

signals.title: Gov Mbah Mourns Late UNN Students, Seeks Ban On Sign-Out Ceremony
signals.summary: [Premium Times] PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the four students were found dead in the lodge on Wednesday.

signals.title: BMH Nurses Urged to Embrace Innovation to Improve Patient Care
signals.summary: [Daily News] Dodoma -- Nurses have been urged to embrace innovative approaches, strengthen communication and promote teamwork to improve patient care and reduce preventable deaths in health facilities.

signals.title: Uganda Moves to Establish Situation Room for Disaster Early Warning, Response
signals.summary: [Nile Post] Uganda is moving to establish a national Situation Room to strengthen disaster preparedness and response, with a new partnership bringing together the Intergovernmental Authority on Development's Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (IGAD-CPAC) and the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR).

signals.title: Amnesty affirme que l'ONU n'a pas empêché un massacre au Soudan du Sud
signals.summary: Un rapport publié par Amnesty International indique que les autorités sud-soudanaises ainsi que la Minuss, la mission de l'ONU au Soudan du Sud, étaient au courant qu'un massacre allait survenir le 1er mars dernier, à Abiemnom. Ce jour-là, 213 personnes perdaient la vie dans une attaque armée. Les Nations unies réfutent ces accusations.

signals.title: News - Drought, Conflict Threaten Emergency-Level Food Insecurity in Tigray, Amhara, Afar
signals.summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Severe drought and escalating conflict are expected to push parts of Tigray, Amhara and Afar into Emergency (IPC Phase 4) levels of food insecurity in early 2027, as widespread crop losses, disrupted markets and declining household purchasing power threaten to deepen an already deteriorating humanitarian situation, according to the Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET).

signals.title: News - 'People Are Getting Desperate': Jimma Protests Expose Growing Anger Over Forced Conscription, Extortion
signals.summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Residents of Jimma city in southwestern Oromia zone in Ethiopia say protests that erupted on Monday and Tuesday were driven by mounting grievances over widespread forced conscription, arbitrary arrests, extortion and displacement, describing an increasingly desperate population with few avenues to seek redress from authorities.

signals.title: UNHRC Calls For Millions in Emergency Aid to Fill Critical Gaps
signals.summary: [allAfrica] Geneva -- The UN Refugee Agency, UNHCR, warned on Tuesday of a deepening crisis that has caused tens of thousands of people to flee from Nigeria to neighbouring Niger and Benin, where problems of malnutrition and disease are surfacing.

signals.title: Ivory Coast Unveils Its Integrated Mineral and Energy Resources Policy
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] Côte d'Ivoire officially unveiled its Integrated Mineral and Energy Policy (PIRME) on November 9, 2026. Spearheaded by President Alassane Ouattara, this ambitious strategy calls for 38,000 billion CFA francs in investments over fifteen years. Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, Minister of Mines, Petroleum, and Energy, unveiled this plan aimed at transforming the national economy.

signals.title: Soudan du Sud : Amnesty accuse l’ONU d’avoir ignoré des alertes avant un massacre
signals.summary: Au Soudan du Sud, Amnesty International accuse les autorités et la mission des Nations unies de ne pas avoir pris les mesures nécessaires pour empêcher un massacre qui a fait plus de 200 morts en mars dernier.

signals.title: Ghana Engages U.S. Civil Rights Lawyer Ben Crump to Seek Justice for Ghanaians Killed in U.S.
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] Approval has been granted to Ghana's Permanent Mission in New York to engage the services of celebrated US civil rights lawyer, Ben Crump, to assist Ghana in securing justice for all Ghanaians killed in the US in recent months.

signals.title: Plusieurs attaques en Éthiopie : le point sur la situation
signals.summary: L'enquête se poursuit en Éthiopie après cette série d'attaques survenue la semaine dernière. Cela s'est passé dans l'ouest du pays, près de la frontière avec le Soudan. Au moins 65 personnes ont été tuées. Parmi elles, 27 civils. Dans cette zone, les affrontements sont devenus monnaie courante. Le point avec le correspondant de France 24 à Addis Abeba, Tom Canetti.

signals.title: Government to Use Big Data to Improve Disaster Preparedness
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- The Mozambican government plans to use artificial intelligence (AI) and Big Data to strengthen disaster preparedness, while prioritizing the expansion of broadband Internet access and the deployment of 5G technology as part of its digital transformation strategy.

signals.title: Gaza Needs 18 Million Meticais to Tackle Drought
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- Mozambique's relief agency, the National Disaster Management Institute (INGD), needs over 18 million meticais (just over 280,000 US dollars at the current exchange rate) to respond to the drought caused by the El Niño phenomenon in southern province of Gaza, which is expected to affect 422,000 households.

signals.title: News - Renewed Fighting in Tigray Pushes Its Fragile Healthcare System Closer to Collapse, Again
signals.summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia has overwhelmed hospitals, disrupted medical services and deepened an already severe healthcare crisis in Tigray, with medical workers warning that civilians increasingly risk being left without access to emergency treatment, according to a report by National Public Radio (NPR).

signals.title: Nsia Banque Ci Net Income Down 27 Percent As of September 2026
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] NSIA Banque Côte d'Ivoire reported a 27% decline in net income, reaching 18.39 billion CFA francs as of the end of September 2026.

signals.title: Drame migratoire au Sénégal : au moins 39 personnes retrouvées mortes
signals.summary: Au moins 39 personnes migrantes sont mortes dans le naufrage de la pirogue qui les transportait, au large du nord-ouest du Sénégal, selon un nouveau bilan annoncé lundi 9 novembre par les autorités. Il s'agit de l'un des drames migratoires les plus meurtriers de ces dernières années au Sénégal. La pirogue a chaviré vendredi 6 novembre dans l'après-midi. Les précisions de Julie Dumont, journaliste à InfoMigrants

signals.title: Major Local Funding for the Doropo Gold Mine in Côte d'Ivoire
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] On November 3 in Abidjan, the Australian mining group Resolute Mining signed financing agreements with seven Ivorian banks. These agreements secure 148 billion CFA francs for the construction of the Doropo gold mine project, located in northeastern Côte d'Ivoire. Led by its subsidiary Doropo Gold Mine SA, this project marks Resolute Mining's first mining operation in the country. It aims to develop a new gold mine approximately 650 kilometers from Abidjan.

signals.title: At Least 56 Migrants Die in Weekend Shipwrecks Off Senegal and Greece

signals.title: Police Kills Three for Alleged Attempt to Rob a Residence
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- On Monday morning, three individuals were shot dead by Mozambican Police (PRM), in Infulene neighborhood, southern municipality of Matola, for allegedly attempting to rob a residence that also serves as a facility of microcredit establishment.

signals.summary: [Daba Finance] Stocks on the West African regional exchange (BRVM) fell in the week ended October 16, 2026, wiping CFA 558.76 billion ($995 million) from market value as 34 of the exchange's 48 listed companies recorded losses. The BRVM Composite Index dropped 2.61% to 532.61 points, while the BRVM-30 declined 2.66% to 257.54 points. The BRVM Prestige Index fell 3.02% to 196.95 points, and the BRVM Principal lost 1.44% to 373.67 points.

signals.title: Ivory Coast Adopts Ambitious 2027 Budget With Targeted 6.6 Percent GDP Growth
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] On October 14, the Council of Ministers of Côte d'Ivoire adopted the 2027 budget bill, as well as the 2025 budget settlement law. These fundamental pieces of legislation govern the country's public finances, marking a key milestone in the development of the government's next budgetary framework. The 2027 budget is balanced at 18,466.1 billion CFA francs in revenue and expenditures, representing a 6.4% increase compared to the previous fiscal year.

signals.title: Malian Army and Rebels Committing Abuses Against Civilians, Rights Group Says
signals.summary: [RFI] The Malian army and its Russian paramilitary allies have killed civilians in violation of international law, Human Rights Watch (HRW) has said in a new report, which also confirms the al-Qaeda-linked jihadist group (JNIM) summarily executed Malian soldiers following an attack on a military convoy in July.

signals.title: Nduhungirehe, Mali President Discuss Bilateral Relations

signals.title: Attack On NDC Supporters in Lagos Cowardly - - Ladipo Johnson

signals.title: Muhoozi Promotes CID Director Magambo to Acting Lt Col

signals.title: Will Uganda's Youth Power the Ai Economy, or Be Left Behind By It?
signals.summary: [Independent (Kampala)] With 13.4 million young people, Uganda has a major stake in the AI revolution. Artificial intelligence could create new opportunities for jobs, enterprise and growth, but a new Commonwealth study warns that gaps in infrastructure, skills and policy could leave the country behind, reports Ronald Musoke.

signals.title: APC Condemns Attacks On Political Gatherings, Calls for Arrest of Perpetrators

signals.title: 2027 - INEC Schedules Mock Accreditation, to Launch New Safeguards
signals.summary: [Premium Times] INEC Chair Joash Amupitan says the exercise would enable the commission to test its accreditation system and electronic transmission of election results ahead of the general elections.

signals.title: Trade, Energy and Regional Peace Dominate Abiy-Erdoğan Talks in Antalya

signals.title: Runda Residents Demand Urgent Limuru Road Pothole Repairs After Head-On Crash
